testName: Air Brakes Test #1 25 Questions • Passing Score 20

questions.question: What is a wig wag?

options.text: A low air pressure warning device.
A tube that carries air to the brakes.
A type of air brake system.

questions.correctAnswerText: A low air pressure warning device.
questions.explanation: A wig wag is a low air pressure warning device. It drops a mechanical arm into the driver's view when air pressure in the tanks drops to between 55 and 75 psi. All vehicles with air brakes must have this device.

questions.question: The ____ turn on when you press the brake pedal.
questions.explanation: Brake lights turn on when you push the brake pedal. An electric switch is triggered by air pressure, which turns on the brake lights.

questions.question: To have normal stopping power, drivers with a front brake limiting valve should:
questions.explanation: Some older vehicles have front brake limiting valves with normal and slippery settings. Set the valve to normal. Setting it to slippery reduces stopping power.

questions.question: Brakes that are out of adjustment will:

options.text: Cause some brakes to overwork and break down.

questions.correctAnswerText: Cause some brakes to overwork and break down.
questions.explanation: Out-of-adjustment brakes will fade faster than properly adjusted brakes. Check brake adjustment often to prevent brake problems.

questions.question: An Anti-Lock Braking System (ABS):

options.text: Is not available for vehicles with air brakes.
Is not helpful in most driving situations.
Helps you stay in control when braking.

questions.correctAnswerText: Helps you stay in control when braking.
questions.explanation: Anti-Lock Braking Systems (ABS) work with air brakes. They help you maintain control by preventing the wheels from locking up when you brake.

questions.question: What type of force do emergency brakes use?
questions.explanation: Air brake systems have three parts: service brake, parking brake, and emergency brake. Emergency and parking brakes use mechanical force.

questions.question: An emergency brake must be controlled by:
questions.explanation: All trucks and buses must have emergency and parking brakes. They must use mechanical force because air pressure can leak away over time.

questions.question: If the safety relief valve releases air from the air brake system:

options.text: The air pressure is too high.

questions.correctAnswerText: The air pressure is too high.
questions.explanation: The safety relief valve releases air when pressure gets too high. If this happens, something is wrong with the system and a mechanic should check it.

questions.question: What do the two systems in a dual air brake system share?
questions.explanation: Both systems in a dual air brake system share one air compressor. If the compressor fails, neither system will work.

questions.question: Brake fade is caused by:
questions.explanation: Overusing brakes causes them to overheat. When brakes get too hot, they fade and become less effective at slowing the vehicle.

questions.question: Brakes can lose adjustment quickly, especially when:
questions.explanation: Hot brakes lose adjustment faster than others. Check your brake adjustment regularly. Your vehicle needs properly working and adjusted brakes to stop safely.

questions.question: Emergency brakes:

options.text: Are not required on vehicles with air brakes.

questions.explanation: All trucks, truck tractors, and buses must have emergency brakes and parking brakes.

questions.question: Which of the following is NOT part of an air brake system?
questions.explanation: An air brake system includes an air compressor, air storage tanks, air tank drains, a safety valve, a brake pedal, foundation brakes, pressure gauges, a low air pressure warning light, spring brakes, and parking brake controls. An air filter is not part of this system.

questions.question: A safety valve opens at ____ pounds per square inch (psi).
questions.explanation: The safety valve prevents too much air pressure from building up in the air tanks and system. It is usually set to open at 150 psi.

questions.question: On flat surfaces, wheel chocks:

options.text: Can stop a parked vehicle from moving.
Make a parked vehicle roll easier.
Should only be used on the front driver's side tire.

questions.correctAnswerText: Can stop a parked vehicle from moving.
questions.explanation: When you cannot use the parking brake, wheel chocks hold a parked vehicle in place on level ground.

questions.question: In a newer vehicle, the parking brake is applied by:

options.text: Moving a lever to the right.

questions.explanation: In newer vehicles with air brakes, the parking brake uses a yellow, diamond-shaped knob. Pull the knob out to apply the parking brakes. Push it in to release them.

questions.question: If you don't drain air tanks, it could cause:

options.text: Water to freeze and cause brake failure.
Too much air in the tanks.

questions.correctAnswerText: Water to freeze and cause brake failure.
questions.explanation: Air tanks must be drained regularly to remove water and compressor oil. Water left in the tanks can freeze in cold weather and cause the brakes to fail.

questions.question: When parked on a flat surface, you should:

options.text: Use wheel chocks to prevent your vehicle from moving.
Use wheel chocks only after you apply the parking brake.

questions.correctAnswerText: Use wheel chocks to prevent your vehicle from moving.
questions.explanation: Always use wheel chocks when parking on level ground. This is essential if your vehicle does not have spring brakes to keep it from rolling.

questions.question: During a static leakage test, what is the maximum safe air leak rate for a double combination vehicle?
questions.explanation: In a static leakage test on a double combination vehicle, the air should leak no more than 3 psi in one minute. If air leaks faster, something needs repair and the vehicle should not be driven.

questions.question: The air compressor is connected to the:
questions.explanation: The air compressor is connected to the engine using gears or a v-belt. It can be air-cooled or cooled by the engine's cooling system.

questions.question: You are braking on dry pavement at 55 mph. How much distance does brake lag add to your total stopping distance?
questions.explanation: Stopping distance has four parts: perception distance, reaction distance, brake lag distance, and braking distance. At 55 mph on dry pavement, brake lag adds about 32 feet to your total stopping distance.

questions.question: What do air brakes use to stop the vehicle?
questions.explanation: Large trucks and buses use air brakes. Air brake systems use compressed air to operate.

questions.question: Vehicles with Anti-Lock Braking Systems (ABS) have ____ warning lights that show when the ABS is not working.
questions.explanation: Vehicles with ABS have yellow warning lights. These lights tell you when the brake system is not working. Know where your warning light is located before you drive.

questions.question: A low air pressure warning signal:

options.text: Is not recommended on vehicles with air brakes.
Is required on vehicles with air brakes.
Is optional on vehicles with air brakes.

questions.correctAnswerText: Is required on vehicles with air brakes.
questions.explanation: All vehicles with air brakes must have a low air pressure warning signal.

questions.question: Why do large vehicles use air brakes?

options.text: Other brake systems squeak too loudly.
Air brakes are very effective systems.
Other braking systems are hard to come by.

questions.correctAnswerText: Air brakes are very effective systems.
questions.explanation: When used and maintained correctly, air brakes are a safe and effective way to stop large, heavy vehicles.
